# agenthub Documentation

What agenthub does, and every endpoint it answers.

> Ships with this console build

## Concepts

agenthub registers five kinds of resource plus a custom lane, then runs them over A2A. Every call resolves to one resource, produces one task, and reports one health value that it actually measured.

### Resource lanes

| Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| Model | A provider behind an OpenAI-compatible chat completions API. |
| Agent | A remote agent that publishes an A2A Agent Card. |
| MCP | An MCP server reached over stdio or streamable HTTP. |
| Skill | A packaged instruction set an agent can load. |
| CLI | A local command, run only when it is on the allowlist. |
| Custom | Anything else you want to register and route to. |

### Task lifecycle

`Submitted → Working → Input required → Completed | Failed | Canceled`

A task parked in input-required waits indefinitely. Resume it with tasks/resume and the same task id.

### Health

**Healthy** · **Degraded** · **Unhealthy** · **Unknown**

A health value is only ever written by a probe or a run. Nothing declares itself healthy, so an unmeasured resource stays unknown.

### Record status

`Draft → Pending → Approved → Rejected | Deprecated`

draft to pending to approved, then deprecated. Only approved records are discoverable and exported.

## A2A methods

A single JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint answers every method below. The HTTP status stays 200 even when the task fails: read result.state, not the status line.

| Method | What it does | Params | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message/send` | Run one turn and wait for the terminal state. | `{ message, configuration?, metadata? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: Task }` |
| `message/stream` | The same turn, with frames streamed as it progresses. | `{ message, configuration?, metadata? }` | `text/event-stream: task_status_update \| task_artifact_update \| message \| task_span_update` |
| `tasks/get` | Read a task together with its history. | `{ id, taskId?, historyLength?, metadata? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: Task }` |
| `tasks/cancel` | Cancel a task that is still running. | `{ id, taskId?, historyLength?, metadata? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: Task }` |
| `tasks/resume` | Answer a task that is parked waiting for input. | `{ id, taskId?, message, metadata? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: Task }` |
| `tasks/pushNotification/set` | Register the callback a task should notify. | `{ taskId, id?, pushNotificationConfig? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: PushNotificationConfig }` |
| `tasks/pushNotification/get` | Read the callback registered for a task. | `{ id, taskId? }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result: PushNotificationConfig }` |

The stream ends on the terminal status frame; there is no sentinel frame after it.

### v0.1 aliases

- `tasks/send` → `message/send`
- `tasks/sendSubscribe` → `message/stream`

### Shapes

**Message**

```json
{
  "kind": "message",
  "role": "user",
  "messageId": "…",
  "parts": [
    { "kind": "text", "type": "text", "text": "probe google-adk" }
  ]
}
```

**Task**

```json
{
  "kind": "task",
  "id": "task-ff5eba3cefe2be87",
  "status": {
    "state": "completed",
    "message": { "role": "agent", "parts": [{ "type": "text", "text": "…" }] }
  },
  "artifacts": [
    { "artifactId": "agent.a2a-0", "name": "agent.a2a", "parts": [{ "type": "data", "data": { … } }] }
  ],
  "history": [{ "role": "user", "parts": [{ "type": "text", "text": "…" }] }]
}
```

## HTTP API

The control plane the console itself talks to. Each route needs a session cookie; the permission column names what the caller must hold.

### Protocol

| Method | Path | Permission | What it does | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/.well-known/agent.json` | — | The A2A Agent Card: where discovery starts. | — | `AgentCard { name, description, url, version, protocolVersion, capabilities, skills[] }` |
| `GET` | `/a2a/agent-card` | — | The same card served on a second path. | — | `AgentCard` |
| `POST` | `/a2a` | — | One JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint carrying every A2A method. | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, method: "message/send", params }` | `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id, result } \| { jsonrpc: "2.0", id, error: { code, message } }` |
| `GET` | `/a2a/stream` | `tasks:read` — Read tasks | Server-sent events for one task. | `?task=<id>&since=<seq>` | `text/event-stream, keep-alive every 15s` |

### Authentication

| Method | Path | Permission | What it does | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/config` | — | What the login screen is allowed to offer. | — | `{ providers: [{ name }], password, registrationOpen, configured }` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/register` | — | Create an account while registration is open. | `{ email, password, name }` | `{ user } — 201` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | — | Trade an email and password for a session cookie. | `{ email, password }` | `{ user } and a session cookie` |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/logout` | — | Drop the session you are using. | — | `204, no body` |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/me` | — | Who you are, and what you are allowed to do. | — | `{ user: { id, email, name, isOwner, roles, groups }, permissions: [] }` |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/sessions` | — | List all sessions | — | `{ sessions: [{ id, createdAt, expiresAt, lastSeenAt, current }] }` |
| `DELETE` | `/api/auth/sessions/{id}` | — | Delete one of the sessions | — | `204, no body` |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/oauth/{provider}` | — | Begin an OAuth round trip. | — | `302 to the provider, PKCE + state` |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/oauth/{provider}/callback` | — | Finish it and land back on the console. | — | `302 to the console with a session cookie` |

| `PUT` | `/api/router/policies/{source}` | `tasks:write` — Cancel and resume tasks | Replace one of the routing rules outright | `{ mode(off\|candidate\|request_only), allow?, keywords?, quietStart?, quietEnd?, resource? }` | `Policy \| 400 router_policy_invalid` |
| `POST` | `/api/router/passes` | `tasks:write` — Cancel and resume tasks | Run one scheduling beat now instead of waiting for the interval. | — | `{ kicked: true } — 202` |
| `GET` | `/api/router/events` | `tasks:read` — Read tasks | SSE: replay from `since`, then follow the scheduler live. | `?since=<seq>&subject=` | `text/event-stream, event name router_event` |

### Audit trail

| Method | Path | Permission | What it does | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/audit` | `audit:read` — Read the audit trail | List all audit events | `?from=&to=&actor=&action=&resource=&source=&outcome=&q=&before=&limit=` | `{ events: AuditEvent[], stats: { total, failed, denied, written }, next }` |
| `GET` | `/api/audit/verify` | `audit:read` — Read the audit trail | Recompute the hash chain over the window and report the first row that does not link. | `?from=&to=` | `{ ok, checked, brokenAt } — brokenAt is the first row whose hash does not link` |
| `GET` | `/api/audit/{id}` | `audit:read` — Read the audit trail | Read one of the audit events by id | — | `AuditEvent { eventId, eventTime, requestId, eventSource, eventName, readOnly, actorKind, actorId, actorLabel, sourceIPAddress, httpMethod, path, resourceId, resourceKind, status, errorCode, latencyMs, userAgent, prevHash, hash }` |

Open a row to see its request and response.

## Authentication and permissions

Identity comes from a session cookie, authorisation from permissions resolved once per request. Per-resource grants narrow this further.

### Sessions

POST /api/auth/login sets an http-only cookie. An OAuth round trip starts at /api/auth/oauth/{provider} and lands back on the callback.

### Sign-up and first login

Self-service sign-up is available when AGENTHUB_ALLOW_REGISTRATION is on. A password must be at least 8 bytes, the address must look like an address, and the first account on an empty instance becomes the owner. Accounts created this way - and accounts a first OAuth login provisions - start on the read-only viewer role: they read the catalogue and nothing more until an administrator widens them. Accounts created through POST /api/users get exactly the roles that were asked for.

### Permissions

A route is guarded by one permission or a list, and any single one of them is enough to enter.

The owner account holds every known permission and bypasses the matrix entirely.

### Groups

A group carries roles and its members inherit them, so naming a group once beats ticking the same roles on every user; a group is also a principal that resource grants can point at. Renaming it or changing its roles takes effect on the next request. Sending roles: [] clears the bundle; omitting the field leaves it alone.

### API keys

A key is a long-lived bearer credential that authenticates as its owner but only with the permissions chosen at creation. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer ahk_…` on /api routes, or as `X-AgentHub-Key`, and on the A2A endpoint.

Scope a key to the least permission it needs; a key can never be granted more than its owner holds. Treat the token as a secret — it is shown once and only its hash is stored.

## Execution sandboxes

Every agent action that touches the outside world runs inside a leased environment. The brain decides; the hands are a container, a user-space kernel, a microVM, a process sandbox or a node you enrolled — the control plane never runs anything as the host process.

| Layer | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `container` | Docker or rootless podman: one namespace-isolated container per lease, read-only root, tmpfs scratch, and no network unless the resource asked for it. The default. |
| `usermode-kernel` | runsc (gVisor) interposes a user-space kernel, so a container escape lands in Go rather than in the host kernel. |
| `microvm` | Kata or Firecracker: a real boundary per lease, at the cost of a boot on creation. |
| `process` | bubblewrap, nsjail, isolate: namespaces and seccomp without a container runtime. Cheaper, and only as strong as the host kernel. |
| `platform` | A hosted runtime (E2B, Daytona, CubeSandbox, OpenHands) reached through a declarative template: no vendor SDK is compiled in. |
| `remote` | A node you enrolled — agentbuddy on your own machine. The server queues a job and the node runs it inside its own root and allowlist. |
| `none` | off refuses every execution. Nothing runs, and the console says so instead of falling back. |

## Errors

Failures answer with a machine-readable code. Grouped here by the HTTP status they map to.

| Status | Meaning | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | Bad Request | `bad_request, weak_password, invalid_email, invalid_grant, unknown_permission, password_required, backup_schedule_invalid, restore_confirm_required, schedule_invalid, router_policy_invalid` |
| `401` | Unauthorized | `unauthorized, unauthenticated, session_expired, invalid_credentials` |
| `403` | Forbidden | `forbidden, user_disabled, builtin_role, skill_distill_disabled` |
| `404` | Not Found | `not_found, backup_not_found, computer_not_found, schedule_not_found, router_ticket_not_found, router_trigger_not_found, router_thread_not_found` |
| `405` | Method Not Allowed | `method_not_allowed` |
| `409` | Conflict | `email_taken, role_already_exists, group_already_exists, backups_disabled, backup_in_progress, backup_checksum_mismatch, backup_schema_mismatch, backup_invalid_archive, router_ticket_closed, router_handback_exhausted, router_resource_unset` |
| `413` | Payload Too Large | `payload_too_large` |
| `500` | Internal Server Error | `internal_error, backup_engine_failed, backup_failed, backup_interrupted, restore_failed` |
| `502` | Bad Gateway | `oauth_not_configured, oauth_state_mismatch, oauth_failed, oauth_no_email` |
| `503` | Service Unavailable | `backup_engine_unavailable, restore_busy, restore_in_progress, feature_unavailable` |

The body is always {"code": "..."}. Log the code rather than any prose that came with it.

### Adapter codes

| Codes | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `resource_unreachable` | The resource never answered. |
| `adapter_timeout` | The call did not come back inside its budget. |
| `provider_malformed` | It answered, but in a shape nothing could use. |
| `provider_unauthorized` | It answered, and rejected the credentials. |
| `cli_command_not_allowed` | The command is missing from the allowlist. |
| `unknown_kind` | No adapter is registered for this kind. |
